name: Maine
$scopeNote: STATE income tax + Paid Family & Medical Leave (PFML, employee AND employer shares, contributions began 2025-01-01, benefits available from 2026-05-01). Maine has NO local income tax anywhere and NO reciprocity agreement with any state -- residents working elsewhere instead claim a RETURN-level credit for taxes paid to another jurisdiction (out of scope, same convention as every other state's return-level credit already disclosed in this project, e.g. Connecticut's).
$methodComment: See maineWithholding()'s own doc comment in src/taxes/state.ts for the full mechanism (phased standard deduction + flat per-allowance amount + progressive bracket, structurally close to Wisconsin's bracketPhaseoutDeduction() but with a genuinely different, easy-to-miss feature: Maine rounds to the nearest WHOLE DOLLAR at multiple intermediate steps, not once at the end -- confirmed against all 3 of the source document's own worked examples, reproduced exactly in tests/engine.test.ts).
exemptPretaxComment: INFERRED, not directly confirmed: Maine's own 2026 withholding instructions explicitly state 'Maine does not conform to the federal deductions that may be used to reduce the required federal withholding amount' -- but that statement is specifically about federal Form W-4 Step 4(b) (the optional itemized-deductions adjustment line), a genuinely DIFFERENT concept from whether pretax elective deferrals (401(k), section 125, etc.) reduce the wage base BEFORE withholding is computed at all. No source found this session directly addresses pretax-deferral conformity either way, so this reuses the federal-conforming exemptPretax list by inference (standard payroll practice, the same conformity pattern as Michigan/Ohio/Idaho/Connecticut/Iowa/Vermont/Massachusetts in this project) rather than PA's non-conforming empty list -- lower confidence than this project's directly-quoted conformity findings for those states.

sources.title: Maine Revenue Services — Withholding Tables for Individual Income Tax (2026)
sources.verifiedBy: Downloaded and text-extracted directly (pdftotext -layout, extracted cleanly, no column-garbling hazard). ENGINE-CONSUMED: the complete 6-step Percentage Method formula, the $5,300 flat per-allowance amount, the phased standard-deduction bands (single: full $12,450 at/below $102,250, $0 at/above $177,250, linear between; married: full $27,750 at/below $204,550, $0 at/above $354,550), both bracket schedules (single: 5.80%/6.75%/7.15% at $0/$27,400/$64,850; married: same rates at $0/$54,850/$129,750), the whole-dollar rounding instruction ('round to the nearest dollar'), the no-form-filed default (single, no allowances), the 3-checkbox marital status shape, and the supplemental-wages rule (aggregate if paid with regular wages; payer MAY withhold a flat 5% if paid separately -- optional, not mandatory). Includes 3 fully worked examples covering both marital statuses and the standard-deduction phase-out band -- reproduced exactly in tests/engine.test.ts, describe('Maine').

sources.title: Form W-4ME, Employee's Withholding Allowance Certificate (Revised: December 2025)
sources.verifiedBy: Downloaded and text-extracted directly (pdftotext -layout), the same 'check the actual form' discipline that caught a real bug in Idaho's build. Confirmed the Personal Allowances Worksheet (Lines A-E: personal, spouse, HOH, dependents, summed into Line 4), Line 5 (additional withholding, matches the existing generic mechanism), and FIVE distinct exemption reasons on Line 6 (federal-W-4-exempt, federal-W-4P-no-withholding, resident-no-prior/current-year-liability, retirement-payee-no-liability, Military Spouse Residency Relief Act) plus a SIXTH, structurally separate one on Line 7 (enrolled tribal member working on tribal land) -- all six collapse to the same $0-withholding engine outcome via the existing generic certificate.exempt mechanism, since this engine does not adjudicate WHICH reason applies, the same eligibility-adjudication scope boundary as every other state's exemption certificate in this project. No undisclosed field found.

sources.title: Maine Department of Labor — June 2026 Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) Employer FAQ
sources.verifiedBy: Downloaded and text-extracted directly (pdftotext -layout). Verbatim: 'For calendar years 2025-2027, the joint contribution rate for employers and employees is set at either 0.5 or 1 percent of wages based on the size of the employer. No more than 0.5 percent can come from the employee. Employers with 15 or more employees will contribute 1 percent of wages and may deduct up to half of the contribution from the employees' wages. Employers with less than 15 employees will contribute 0.5 percent of wages and may deduct the entire amount from the employees' wages.' Wage base: 'excludes amounts above the annual base limit set by the U.S. Social Security Administration.' Modeled as a flat 0.5% employee rate (the maximum either tier may charge, matching every payroll provider's own described practice) plus a 0.5% employer share ONLY for the 15+-employee tier (reusing Washington's exact existing statePaidLeaveEmployee/Employer mechanism with zero new code, since 1.0% total × 50% employee-share-fraction = 0.5% happens to fit that shape precisely) -- see knownGaps for the disclosed small-employer discretion this simplification doesn't capture.

reciprocity.note: Maine has no reciprocity agreement with any state -- cross-source confirmed. Residents working elsewhere claim a return-level 'Credit for Income Tax Paid to Other Jurisdiction' instead, per Maine Revenue Services' own guide (maine.gov/revenue) -- out of scope for this per-paycheck withholding engine, same convention as every other state's return-level credit mechanism already disclosed in this project.

knownGaps: PFML employer-size discretion: Maine's own FAQ confirms employers under 15 employees have a LOWER total required contribution (0.5%, vs 1.0% for 15+) and MAY deduct the entire amount from the employee -- meaning a small employer could legally choose to absorb some or all of that 0.5% themselves, making the employee's ACTUAL withholding potentially less than the 0.5% this file assumes as the (most common, per every payroll provider surveyed) default. This engine has no certificate field to represent 'this small employer chose to absorb part of the premium' -- disclosed rather than silently assumed exact.

Local income tax absence is standard general knowledge / cross-source only, not independently confirmed against a specific Maine statute or constitutional provision the way Massachusetts's prohibition was (see that file's own constitutional citations) -- a real, disclosed access-depth difference between these two neighboring files.

Supplemental wages paid on a SEPARATE cheque: Maine's own instructions make the flat-5% method OPTIONAL for this case ('the payer MAY withhold a flat five percent'), not mandatory -- this engine's default (aggregation via taxableWagesFor(), the same as every other state without a distinct supplemental method) reflects the OTHER path Maine's own instructions describe (paid WITH regular wages), and cannot look back at a prior separate cheque regardless -- same disclosed class of gap as Kentucky/Idaho/Connecticut/Iowa.

The tribal-member exemption (Form W-4ME Line 7) is scoped narrowly to wages earned FOR WORK PERFORMED ON TRIBAL LAND specifically -- this engine's generic certificate.exempt flag applies to the WHOLE paycheck, so a caller representing a tribal member with SOME Maine wages earned off tribal land would need to model that split outside this engine (the same scope boundary as every eligibility-adjudication gate in this project, but worth naming since the underlying exemption is itself income-source-scoped, not simply person-scoped).
